questions.prompt: In a directed acyclic graph (DAG), which of the following best describes a confounder?

options.text: A variable that lies on the causal pathway from the treatment to the outcome.
A variable that is a descendant of the outcome.
A variable that causes both the treatment and the outcome.
A variable that is only affected by the treatment.

questions.explanation: A confounder causes both the treatment and the outcome, creating a spurious association if not controlled for.

questions.prompt: The backdoor adjustment criterion requires that we adjust for a set of variables that blocks all backdoor paths between the treatment and the outcome. Which condition must be satisfied for a set to be a valid backdoor adjustment set?

options.text: The set must contain at least one collider.
The set must block every path that starts with an arrow pointing into the treatment.
The set must include all descendants of the treatment.
The set must contain only variables that are causes of the outcome.

questions.explanation: A backdoor set blocks every path that begins with an arrow into the treatment, thereby removing confounding bias.
